g1.flow: Two versions of 'your Lord is most knowing of who strays'. Al-Anʿām 6:117 says man yaḍillu (who strays), after a warning that obeying most people on earth would mislead you. Al-Qalam 68:7 says bi-man ḍalla (who has gone astray), after 'which of you is the afflicted'. Hook: the earlier surah keeps the verb ongoing, yaḍillu; the later one has it done, ḍalla.

cues.6:117: Man yaḍillu, no bi-: follows 'obey most on earth and they will mislead you.'
cues.68:7: Bi-man ḍalla: follows 'which of you is the afflicted'; next, 'do not obey the deniers.'

g2.flow: Word for word the same. Al-Qalam 68:15 describes a man who has 'wealth and children', and the next ayah threatens to brand his snout. Al-Muṭaffifīn 83:13 follows 'none deny it except every sinful transgressor', and the next ayah is 'No! The stain has covered their hearts.' Hook: wealth and snout in Al-Qalam; sin and stain in Al-Muṭaffifīn.

cues.68:15: After 'possessor of wealth and children'; next, 'We will brand him upon the snout.'
cues.83:13: After 'none deny it except every sinful transgressor'; next, 'No! The stain covers their hearts.'

g3.flow: Identical words, each finishing a lament. Al-Wāqiʿah 56:67 completes 'we are in debt', then the surah moves on to 'the water that you drink'. Al-Qalam 68:27 completes 'when they saw it: we are lost', then the most moderate of them speaks. Hook: debt in Al-Wāqiʿah, lost in Al-Qalam; the Qalam group keeps talking, the Wāqiʿah scene ends.

cues.56:67: Finishes 'we are in debt'; next ayah asks about the water you drink.
cues.68:27: Finishes 'when they saw it: we are lost'; next, the most moderate of them speaks.

g4.flow: Four scenes of people turning to one another. Aṣ-Ṣāffāt 37:27: those in surrender that Day. 37:50: after 'well-protected eggs'. Aṭ-Ṭūr 52:25: after 'pearls well-protected'. Al-Qalam 68:30: after 'we were wrongdoers', and only here it ends yatalāwamūn (blaming); the others end yatasāʾalūn. Hook: the opening word alternates in muṣḥaf order: wa-aqbala, fa-aqbala, wa-aqbala, fa-aqbala.

cues.37:27: Wa-aqbala … yatasāʾalūn, after 'that Day, in surrender'; next, 'you came at us from the right.'
cues.37:50: Fa-aqbala … yatasāʾalūn, after 'as if delicate eggs'; next, 'I had a companion.'
cues.52:25: Wa-aqbala … yatasāʾalūn, after boys 'like pearls well-protected'; next, 'we were fearful among our people.'
cues.68:30: Fa-aqbala … yatalāwamūn (blaming), right after 'Exalted is our Lord! We were wrongdoers.'

g5.flow: Same cry, different last word. Al-Anbiyāʾ 21:14 ends ẓālimīn (wrongdoers), after the people are told not to flee but return to their luxury. Al-Qalam 68:31 ends ṭāghīn (transgressors): 'we were wrongdoers' was already said two ayat earlier at 68:29, so here the word is transgressors. Hook: Al-Anbiyāʾ says ẓālimīn; Al-Qalam goes from wrongdoers to ṭāghīn.

cues.21:14: Ends ẓālimīn; after 'do not flee, return to your luxury and homes.'
cues.68:31: Ends ṭāghīn; right after they blame each other, just past 'we were wrongdoers.'

g6.flow: Same words in both, each after a 'this versus that' question. Aṣ-Ṣāffāt 37:154 follows 'has He chosen daughters over sons?'. Al-Qalam 68:36 follows 'will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?'. After it, Aṣ-Ṣāffāt asks 'will you not be reminded?' while Al-Qalam asks 'or do you have a scripture?'. Hook: daughters and sons in Aṣ-Ṣāffāt; Muslims and criminals in Al-Qalam.

cues.37:154: After 'has He chosen daughters over sons?'; next, 'will you not be reminded?'
cues.68:36: After 'will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?'; next, 'or do you have a scripture?'

g7.flow: Identical, and the ayah before is nearly the same too: deniers led on 'from where they do not know'. Al-Aʿrāf 7:183: 'those who deny Our signs', then 'no madness in their companion'. Al-Qalam 68:45: 'leave Me with whoever denies this statement', then the 'or' questions begin: 'or do you ask of them a payment?'. Hook: signs in Al-Aʿrāf, statement in Al-Qalam.

cues.7:183: Before: 'those who deny Our signs'; next, 'no madness in their companion.'
cues.68:45: Before: 'leave Me with whoever denies this statement'; next, 'or do you ask a payment?'

g8.flow: Identical, and in both surahs the next ayah is the same too: 'or have they the unseen, so they write it down?'. The difference is around the pair. Aṭ-Ṭūr 52:40 follows 'has He daughters while you have sons?', and a plan is mentioned after the pair. Al-Qalam 68:46 follows 'My plan (kaydī) is firm'. Hook: in Al-Qalam the plan comes before; in Aṭ-Ṭūr, after.

cues.52:40: After 'has He daughters while you have sons?'; part of a long run of 'or' questions.
cues.68:46: Right after 'I will give them time; My plan (kaydī) is firm.'

g9.flow: Identical, and always straight after the 'payment' ayah. Aṭ-Ṭūr 52:41 keeps the 'or' questions going: 'or do they intend a plan?'. Al-Qalam 68:47 ends the questions and turns to the Prophet ﷺ: 'be patient, and be not like the companion of the fish'. Hook: Aṭ-Ṭūr keeps asking; Al-Qalam turns to patience and Jonah.

cues.52:41: After the payment question; next, 'or do they intend a plan?'
cues.68:47: After the payment question; next, 'be patient, not like the companion of the fish.'

g10.flow: Three times 'a reminder to the worlds'. Ṣād 38:87 and At-Takwīr 81:27 open with in huwa; only Al-Qalam 68:52 opens with wa-mā huwa, as the surah's last ayah, straight after 'they say, indeed he is mad'. Muṣḥaf order: Ṣād, Al-Qalam, At-Takwīr. Hook: in, wa-mā, in; the odd one sits in the middle.

cues.38:87: In huwa; after 'I ask you no payment, and I am not pretentious.'
cues.68:52: Wa-mā huwa; last ayah of the surah, after 'they say, indeed he is mad.'
cues.81:27: In huwa; after 'so where are you going?'; next, 'for whoever wills… a right course.'
